properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Source: the SECOND half of Alex Sligar's 2026-08-05 exchange, relayed by Anthony 2026-08-06. In Alex's own words, the use case is: "I have a ton of domain/tribal knowledge about my project, beyond the code itself. For example, I know why certain UI sections were created or have talked with the users and want a better way to document this information for junior devs on my project. I'd like to brain dump a bunch of this info in a way that other devs can query it using an AI prompt." STILL OPEN.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A NODE RATHER THAN A NOD: Alex described reflow2's use case almost exactly — rationale, who asked for it, what constraint drove it, kept beside the code and queryable in natural language — and the research answered him with Notion AI, Confluence/Rovo and Cognee. reflow2 was not a candidate in an answer to the question reflow2 exists to answer. Whatever else is true, that is a finding.

WHAT REFLOW2 ALREADY HAS FOR IT: add_decision with a rationale, authored_by (whose word this is), the golden thread from requirement to capability to artifact, and search_design over all of it. Against a wiki it has one property no wiki has: a rationale in reflow2 can be shown to have gone STALE, because the thing it justified is linked and drift is computed. A Confluence page saying "the legacy report screen stays because finance uses it monthly" stays confidently wrong forever after finance stops. That is the same normative property recorded in dec:idea-normative-vs-descriptive-graph, seen from the tribal-knowledge angle.

THE TENSION, and it is with an ACCEPTED requirement, not a soft one: req:driving-agent states that the primary consumers are coding agents and "the human is reached only through the agent". Alex's junior dev is a human asking a question with no build task attached and no design intent to capture. Serving that reader well means a read-optimised, question-answering surface — closer to Q&A over the graph than to the capture-detect-ask-decide loop — and the loop is what the current skill kit is built around. It is a different product surface on the same store, which is either a natural projection (dec:views-are-projections would allow it, since answering from the graph invents nothing) or a second product, and those have very different costs.

WHAT IS CHEAP: nothing new is needed to try it. An agent with the existing read tools can already answer "why does this exist" from a well-populated graph. The cheap experiment is to have someone who did not build the design ask it questions and see what it cannot answer.

WHAT IS EXPENSIVE, AND THE HONEST OBJECTION: this reader wants to BRAIN DUMP first and get structure later, which is the opposite of the capture loop's order. cap:ingest and cap:corpus-ingest exist for exactly that shape, so the primitive is there — but the loop's habit of asking about gaps at capture time is precisely what a brain-dumping user will experience as friction, and the brainstorm skill's own rule (do not run detect-and-ask over material the user deliberately left soft) exists because of that. Whether a dump-then-structure mode is a mode, a skill, or a different reader's whole path is unsettled.

A CONCRETE DOGFOODING OPPORTUNITY, recorded because it is testable rather than arguable: Alex has the project, the tribal knowledge and the junior devs. Pointing reflow2 at his brain dump would test cap:ingest, the newcomer-query path and the tribal-knowledge story at once, on a design nobody in this repo authored. Anthony's word needed on whether that is wanted.
properties.name: OPEN — is a human newcomer asking "why does this exist" a first-class reader of the graph, when req:driving-agent says the human is reached only through the agent?
properties.rationale: Recorded as an idea because the tension is with an accepted requirement and therefore cannot be resolved by an agent — either req:driving-agent is narrower than it reads, or this reader is out of scope, and only Anthony can say which. Also recorded because the finding that prompted it (reflow2 absent from an answer to its own question) is the kind of thing that vanishes from a conversation and cannot be rediscovered.
